blocks.text: Engineering Showdown: GOJO TFX 1200 mL vs. Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL

For well over a decade, the GOJO TFX vs. Rubbermaid AutoFoam debate has defined commercial restroom soap standardization across US corporate offices, medical clinics, and industrial headquarters. Both fixtures are wall-mounted, infrared-activated, ADA-compliant touchless foaming hand soap dispensers engineered to eliminate cross-contamination at the washbasin while keeping nightly janitorial restroom service ($15 to $30 per restroom per visit) fast and predictable.

Yet a look at the nominal fluid volume misleads many first-time buyers. The GOJO TFX cartridge holds 1,200 mL of foam soap concentrate, while the Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam pouch holds 1,100 mL. Despite holding 100 mL less liquid, the Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL pouch yields up to 2,750 handwashes compared to roughly 2,000 handwashes from a GOJO TFX 1,200 mL bottle. That 37.5% higher dose yield stems from pump calibration: Rubbermaid's integrated pouch valve dispenses a concentrated 0.4 mL aerated micro-foam shot, whereas the GOJO TFX pump dispenses approximately 0.6 mL per trigger.

blocks.text: Flexible Pouch vs. Collapsible Bottle: Trash Volume and Nozzle Hygiene

Inside the cabinet, the two systems handle fluid delivery through different packaging technologies. The Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1100 mL Touchless Soap Dispenser accepts a boxless, hermetically sealed 1,100 mL mylar-style flexible bag with a pre-attached foaming pump valve. As the dispenser's internal cam compresses the pump, atmospheric pressure flattens the flexible pouch completely—leaving almost zero residual soap clinging to container walls and collapsing flat into a trash bag so empty refills occupy 80% less space in the janitor barrel.

The GOJO TFX uses GOJO's Smart-Flex collapsible PET bottle with a rigid neck collar and removable recyclable pump. One operational advantage of the GOJO TFX architecture is its translucent skylight on the top curvature of the dispenser hood: overhead commercial recessed LED lighting shines directly through the top of the clear bottle, allowing a night custodian earning $35 to $65 per hour to spot a low reservoir from across the restroom without opening the housing.

blocks.title: Annual Soap Case Math for a 150-Employee Office Floor
blocks.text: In a 150-employee office operating 255 workdays per year at 3 handwashes per employee per day (114,750 annual handwashes), a GOJO TFX system (2,000 doses/refill, 2-pack or 4-pack cases) consumes 57.4 refills per year. The Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL system (2,750 doses/refill, 4-pack case = 11,000 doses) consumes 41.7 refills per year—saving nearly 16 cartridge changeouts and 4 full cases of soap annually.
Coordinating Your Restroom & Breakroom Consumables Stack

To keep total facility cleaning costs predictable—whether your building falls into the 2,500–9,999 sq ft bracket ($0.09 to $0.15/sq ft) or the 10,000–24,999 sq ft bracket ($0.07 to $0.12/sq ft)—procurement directors pair high-yield touchless foam dispensers with commercial-grade tissue, folded towels, and puncture-resistant can liners:

items: Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1100 mL Touchless Soap Dispenser: Delivers up to 2,750 handwashes per 1,100 mL pouch with a 3-year battery life rating and ADA-compliant touchless actuation.

Scott Pro High-Capacity Coreless Standard Roll Dispenser: Holds 4 coreless bath tissue rolls inside a keyed or keyless ADA-compliant cabinet, matching AutoFoam's extended service interval inside high-traffic restroom stalls.
Tork Universal Multifold Hand Towels Natural (16-Pack Case): Supplies 4,000 100%-recycled 9.125 x 9.5 inch sheets (16 packs of 250) for wall-mounted folded towel dispensers next to the washbasin.
Tork Universal Jumbo Bath Tissue 2-Ply (12-Case): Provides twelve 1,000-foot, 9-inch diameter 2-ply EcoLogo-certified jumbo rolls for facilities running open-market JRT stall dispensers.

Berry Rhino-X 38x60 Heavy-Duty 55-Gallon Liners (200-Case): Engineered from 17-micron high-density polyethylene for leak-proof performance in breakroom wet waste (where breakroom sanitation runs $12 to $25 per visit) and heavy paper towel receptacles.

blocks.text: Battery Lifecycle Management and Preventive Maintenance Protocols

Both the GOJO TFX and Rubbermaid AutoFoam run on standard alkaline C-cell batteries (3 C-cells for GOJO TFX; 4 C-cells for Rubbermaid AutoFoam). In buildings cleaned 3x/week (13.0 visits/month) or 5x/week (21.65 visits/month), dead dispenser batteries are one of the leading causes of tenant facility tickets—often mistaken for an empty soap pouch.

Because the Rubbermaid AutoFoam houses four C-cell batteries driving a low-amperage gear pump rated for up to 3 years or 120,000 cycles, property managers can put battery swaps on an annual or biennial preventive maintenance calendar rather than waiting for the red LED warning light to flash. With the GOJO TFX, night leads should log battery install dates on a strip of painter's tape inside the backplate and replace all three C-cells every 12 to 15 months using industrial alkaline cells (never mixing old and new batteries).

items.name: Step 1: Check Countertop & Mirror Sightline Clearances
items.text: Mount either dispenser at least 8 inches above the vanity deck or sink rim so infrared sensors do not bounce off wet porcelain or chrome faucets.

items.name: Step 2: Load Industrial Alkaline C-Cells and Label the Install Date
items.text: Insert 4 C-cells (Rubbermaid AutoFoam) or 3 C-cells (GOJO TFX) and write the month/year on the interior chassis with a permanent marker for your janitorial supervisor's quarterly audit.

items.name: Step 3: Snap the Sealed Nozzle Cartridge Into the Yoke Collar
items.text: Verify the foaming pump nozzle clicks flush into the lower actuator fork before closing the front hood; an improperly seated nozzle collar is the primary cause of weak or half-shot foam delivery.

faqs.q: Why does the Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL pouch yield more handwashes than the GOJO TFX 1200 mL refill?
faqs.a: The Rubbermaid AutoFoam pump valve is calibrated to dispense 0.4 mL of concentrated liquid soap aerated into a dense micro-foam lather, yielding up to 2,750 doses per 1,100 mL pouch. The GOJO TFX dispenses roughly 0.6 mL per actuation, yielding approximately 2,000 doses from a 1,200 mL cartridge.

faqs.q: Are GOJO TFX and Rubbermaid AutoFoam soap refills interchangeable?
faqs.a: No. GOJO TFX uses a rigid collapsible bottle with a cylindrical GOJO pump collar, while Rubbermaid AutoFoam uses a flat laminated flexible pouch with a proprietary keyed pump nozzle. You must match the refill SKU to the installed dispenser brand.

faqs.q: Has the GOJO TFX been discontinued in favor of the GOJO PURELL ES8?
faqs.a: No. While GOJO actively markets the newer ES8 (Energy-on-the-Refill) and ES6 platforms for new installations, the GOJO TFX remains widely deployed across tens of thousands of US commercial buildings, and genuine GOJO TFX 1200 mL foam refills remain in full commercial production.

faqs.q: How do janitorial contracts bill for touchless soap refills and C-cell battery replacements?
faqs.a: Under a turnkey consumables add-on ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit), the janitorial contractor supplies all foam soap cartridges, paper products, and trash liners, while routine restocking and battery checks are included inside the $15 to $30 per restroom per visit service rate.
